body.statement: For every \(m\in\mathcal M_3\) with \(D(P_m)\neq0\), \(\mathcal Z_{\mathrm{res}}(P_m)=\{(a(m),d(m))\}\) over \(\mathbb C\), the residual ideal equals \(\langle\alpha-a(m),\delta-d(m)\rangle\), and the chart-induced observable functional is well defined and satisfies \[\theta(P_m)=\left(-\frac{s_0(P_m)}{s_1(P_m)},\frac{t_{P_m}(-s_0(P_m)/s_1(P_m))}{l_{P_m}(-s_0(P_m)/s_1(P_m))}\right)^\top=\theta(m).\]
body.justification: It gives an explicit finite-order recovery map and excludes every nontrue complex branch, which a local rank argument cannot do.
body.gap: Tramontano, Drton, and Etesami give partial cyclic full-law results; Mesters and Zwiernik recover full mixing under stronger tensor zeros; neither gives this sparse rational inverse.
body.consumer: A path-dependent overlapping-cycle analysis can report \((a,d)\) from second and third observed cumulants while treating the middle equation as unrestricted nuisance.
